Sequences, regular expressions and characters

Source: R/sequences.R
z3_sequences.Rd

Z3 sequences are finite lists over any element sort; strings are sequences of characters. The string functions (z3_length(), z3_concat(), z3_contains(), z3_prefixof(), z3_suffixof(), z3_substr(), z3_str_at(), z3_indexof(), z3_replace()) work on any sequence.

Usage

z3_seq_sort(element)

z3_re_sort(seq_sort)

z3_char_sort(ctx)

z3_sort_basis(sort)

z3_seq_empty(sort)

z3_seq_unit(x)

z3_seq_nth(s, i)

z3_last_indexof(s, t)

z3_replace_all(s, t, dst)

z3_replace_re(s, re, dst)

z3_replace_re_all(s, re, dst)

z3_seq_power(s, n)

z3_seq_map(f, s)

z3_seq_mapi(f, i, s)

z3_seq_foldl(f, acc, s)

z3_seq_foldli(f, i, acc, s)

z3_re(s)

z3_in_re(s, re)

z3_re_star(re)

z3_re_plus(re)

z3_re_option(re)

z3_re_complement(re)

z3_re_union(...)

z3_re_concat(...)

z3_re_intersect(...)

z3_re_diff(re1, re2)

z3_re_loop(re, lo, hi)

z3_re_power(re, n)

z3_re_range(lo, hi, ctx = NULL)

z3_re_empty(sort)

z3_re_full(sort)

z3_re_allchar(sort)

z3_char_val(ctx, code)

z3_char_to_int(x)

z3_char_to_bv(x)

z3_char_from_bv(x)

z3_char_is_digit(x)

z3_char_le(x, t)

z3_str_from_code(x)

z3_str_to_code(x)

Arguments

element, sort, seq_sort

Sorts.

ctx

A z3_context().

x

An element, character, or Int expression.

s, t, dst

Sequence (or string) expressions.

i, n

Int expressions or R whole numbers.

re, re1, re2

Regular expressions (or strings).

f

An array-valued function (for example a z3_lambda()).

acc

Initial accumulator for folds.

...

Regular expressions or strings.

lo, hi

Bounds: single-character strings for z3_re_range(), counts for z3_re_loop().

code

A Unicode code point.

Value

A z3_expr or z3_sort.

Details

  • Sorts: z3_seq_sort(element), z3_re_sort(seq_sort), z3_char_sort(ctx), and z3_sort_basis() for the element sort.

  • Sequences: z3_seq_empty(sort), z3_seq_unit(x) (one element), z3_seq_nth(s, i) (element i, 0-based), z3_last_indexof(s, t) (Z3 before 4.8.15 misses a match at the last position), z3_replace_all() (Z3 4.15.5), z3_seq_power(s, n) (s repeated n times, Z3 5.3.0), and the higher-order z3_seq_map(), z3_seq_mapi(), z3_seq_foldl(), z3_seq_foldli() (Z3 4.13.2), whose function argument is an array such as one made with z3_lambda().

  • Regular expressions: z3_re() turns a string (or sequence) into a regular expression matching exactly it; z3_in_re(s, re) tests membership. Combinators: z3_re_star(), z3_re_plus(), z3_re_option(), z3_re_union(), z3_re_concat(), z3_re_intersect(), z3_re_complement(), z3_re_diff() (Z3 4.8.14), z3_re_loop(re, lo, hi), z3_re_power(re, n) (Z3 4.8.15), z3_re_range("a", "z", ctx) (a character range), and the constants z3_re_empty(), z3_re_full() and z3_re_allchar() of a regular expression sort. Where a regular expression is expected, a string is accepted and converted with z3_re(). z3_replace_re() and z3_replace_re_all() replace matches (Z3 4.15.5); Z3's solver is incomplete for these and may answer "unknown".

  • Characters: z3_char_val(ctx, code) (Z3 4.8.15), z3_char_to_int(), z3_char_to_bv(), z3_char_from_bv(), z3_char_is_digit(), z3_char_le(), and z3_str_from_code(), z3_str_to_code() (Z3 4.8.15) between one-character strings and code points.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
s <- z3_string(ctx, "s")
digits <- z3_re_plus(z3_re_range("0", "9", ctx))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_in_re(s, z3_re_concat("id-", digits)), z3_length(s) == 6)
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(sol), s))
#> [1] "id-000"

I <- z3_int_sort(ctx)
q <- z3_const(ctx, "q", z3_seq_sort(I))
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_length(q) == 3, z3_seq_nth(q, 0) == 7,
       z3_contains(q, z3_concat(z3_seq_unit(z3_int_val(ctx, 1)), z3_seq_unit(z3_int_val(ctx, 2)))))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_eval(z3_model(sol), q)
#> <z3_expr (Seq Int)> (seq.++ (seq.unit 7) (seq.unit 1) (seq.unit 2))
